answers.rationale: The requirement for integrated power and cooling infrastructure aligns with the capabilities of the CLOUD-INT product, which provides rack-scale integration of compute, power, and cooling systems. This product is suitable for large-scale deployments like an AI training campus.

The IT capacity requirement of 48 MW critical load is a specification detail that informs the design but does not directly map to a specific product. This will be addressed in the overall system design.
The redundancy requirement specifies the design criteria for the power and cooling systems but does not directly map to a specific product. This will be incorporated into the system architecture.

The preference for 800VDC rack-level distribution aligns with the FPM-800V product, which provides DC/DC modules and intermediate bus converters for 800 VDC distribution, suitable for high-power AI infrastructure.

The requirement for 120 kW rack density with liquid cooling at rack and chip level matches the capabilities of JETCOOL-PLATE for direct-to-chip cooling and JETCOOL-CDU for coolant distribution units sized for high-density racks.
The site location and grid interconnect are project-specific details that do not directly map to a product. These will be considered during the project planning and execution phases.
Compliance requirements such as UL, IEC 61439, and NEC Article 645 are standards that the selected products and systems must adhere to, but they do not directly map to a specific product.

The preference for prefabricated/modular systems aligns with the ANORD-POD product, which provides prefabricated modular power pods for fast deployment, suitable for large-scale projects like an AI training campus.
The scope requested specifies the extent of the project but does not directly map to a specific product. This will guide the selection and integration of products and services.
